lines.text: Midwinter came. The sun barely rose. And on the longest night of the year, the wolves came out of the Pale.
Lord Lucan! Wolves on the ridge! Not one or two. A pack. Twenty, maybe more!
Frost-wolves only hunt in packs when they're starving. Something in the Pale had driven them south. Toward us.
Everyone who can hold a spear, to the palisade! Everyone else, into the keep!
I couldn't fight. So I did the only useful thing I could. I counted, and I gave orders.
Tobin, the lamps! Hang them on the wall, frost-wolves hate the light. Wren, archers on the gatehouse. Bram, the barn. They'll go for the goats first.
They hit the palisade like a white wave.
Wren's first arrow killed the lead wolf at a hundred paces. Her second went through two.
Tobin swung his hammer, and a wolf the size of a pony flew backwards over the wall.
Hold the line! Hold it! By the gods. Where did you people learn to fight like knights?
Morale!
Ash took the biggest of them alone, at the gate. It was over in seconds.
And then one got past the wall. It went for the youngest of the goatherds, a boy of nine.
Bram got there first. One arm, one old sword, and fifty years of soldiering.
He cut it down with a single stroke.
By dawn, the wolves were gone. Nineteen dead in the snow. Not one of ours.
Nineteen frost-wolf hearts. Nineteen pieces of rimeglass. Seven hundred and sixty crowns, lying in the snow.
I tried to laugh. Instead, I fell over.
I woke three days later, burning with fever, my fingertips white with frostbite, though I had never left the keep.
You collapsed on the wall, my lord. The healer says it was the cold.
Strange. I was wearing two cloaks.
Beside my bed sat the scholar. She wasn't writing anything down this time. She was just looking at me.
Rest, my lord. You did a great deal of work that night.
I only gave orders.
Yes. I suppose that's one word for it.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter seven, coming soon.
